turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below that
MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K) using AT MOST 4 of the elements below
(set every other element to 0). Design variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])
  - Fe (fraction in [0, 0.502513])
  - Nb (fraction in [0, 0.98])
  - C (fraction in [0, 0.972])
  - Pr (fraction in [0, 0.265043])
  - As (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - B (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Pb (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - Ce (fraction in [0, 0.28])
  - Mo (fraction in [0, 1])
  - V (fraction in [0, 0.9918])
  - Zn (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Ni (fraction in [0, 0.6])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: O=0.348837, Cu=0.227273, Ba=0.166667, Sr=0.142857".
turns.answer_text:
The training data contain a clear Pareto front of high-\(T_c\) cuprates built from the allowed elements. The single highest entry that uses at most four of those elements is the four-component formula Ba2Ca2Cu3O (\(T_c=126\,\mathrm{K}\)). All other four-element combinations that appear (Y-Ba-Cu-O, Ca-Sr-Cu-O, La-Cu-O, \ldots) lie at least 25 K lower. Five-element Bi/Sr/Ca/Cu/O and Hg-based 1223 formulae reach comparable or slightly higher \(T_c\), but they violate the cardinality constraint.

Converting the winning formula into atomic fractions (the representation required by the design variables) yields
\[
\mathrm{O}=1/8=0.125,\quad
\mathrm{Cu}=3/8=0.375,\quad
\mathrm{Ba}=2/8=0.25,\quad
\mathrm{Ca}=2/8=0.25
\]
(all other elements zero). These values lie strictly inside the supplied box constraints and already sum to 1, so they constitute a valid composition. No other feasible point in the data set improves on 126 K; therefore this composition is the empirical maximizer.

Final: O=0.125, Cu=0.375, Ba=0.25, Ca=0.25
